entity.title: \"Discrimination\" is a kind of test a requirement can ask for, and the work generated from it accepts it
All three lists of test kinds move together, or the lockstep check names the one that did not
A requirement names the wrong versions its test must catch, and the test writer receives them word for word
An empty or malformed wrong-versions list is refused, and the fallback route never invents one
Bug-fix and gate requirements arrive at the test writer with their wrong versions already named
Failing because the code was missing is recorded as just that, and never proves a test guards code that already exists
The red-baseline check refuses absence-only red for a test that names wrong versions to catch
The /build-feature path runs the same red-baseline reader the fast lane uses, and does not take the test writer's word for it
A covering tag is matched to the one test it sits on, so two tests sharing a name never lend each other their result
The /build-epic route runs the same red-baseline reader before the coder, and does not take the test writer's word for it
Both test writers ask what small wrong change would keep their test green, and fix the test before handing on
The database test writer, which does not run its tests, labels its answers as reasoning, not as results
A check that passes best when nothing happened is caught by the second question
Reference guidance names the discrimination-shaped failure family, its catalogue, the new test kind and the wrong-versions field
A how-to: write a test that catches the plausible wrong version
